era_benchmark_plan.benchmark_rationale: SPY is the canonical large-cap equity benchmark for a STOCKS sleeve strategy. The thesis mimics regime-aware momentum on equities, so SPY provides a fair passive baseline: it captures the same broad market exposure the strategy is trying to beat, and the known-good momentum template previously used SPY as its explicit benchmark. Using SPY also ensures the regime filter (SPY 200-day SMA, accepted via clarification default) is directly observable against the benchmark itself.

eras.label: Late-cycle bull market (pre-COVID)
eras.rationale: Tests momentum performance in a sustained low-volatility bull environment with a sharp drawdown at the tail (Q4 2018 correction). Validates that the regime filter correctly stays engaged during trending conditions and exits before the COVID shock.

eras.label: COVID crash and V-shaped recovery
eras.rationale: Stress-tests the SPY 200-SMA regime filter under a rapid drawdown and equally rapid recovery. Momentum strategies are known to suffer in whipsaw environments; this era checks whether the filter suppresses entries during the crash and re-engages cleanly on recovery.

eras.label: Rate-hike bear market
eras.rationale: The 2022 bear market is the most important stress era for a regime-aware momentum strategy: SPY spent extended periods below its 200-SMA, which should suppress entries. This era validates that the regime filter materially reduces drawdown versus an unfiltered momentum approach.

eras.label: Post-bear recovery and AI bull
eras.rationale: A strong trending bull market driven by AI-related flows. Momentum strategies historically perform well here. This era validates that the strategy captures upside when the regime filter is engaged and the universe is trending.

eras.label: Recent validation window
eras.rationale: The most recent window checks whether the strategy remains relevant under current market conditions, including the tariff-driven volatility of early 2025. Required as a recency gate before any promotion decision.

trial_ledger_budget.rationale: Sweep space is defined by three lookback windows (20, 60, 120 days) × three stop-loss levels (5%, 10%, 15%) × three profit-target levels (10%, 20%, 30%) = 27 total variants. Four eras span the 2018-01-01 to 2026-05-05 window (pre-COVID bull, COVID crash/recovery, 2022 bear, 2023-2026 recovery). 27 variants × 4 eras = 108 bench runs, which is within the max_bench_runs ceiling. Compute cost is set to 0 because all signals are OHLCV-derived from the wired alpaca_equity_ohlcv feed and no external data pulls incur marginal cost at this tier. Budget is conservative: no additional variant axes are permitted without operator approval, consistent with the known-good momentum template and SMALL capital tier constraints. Server normalization: Server raised the trial-ledger budget to cover 27 variants across 5 eras after sectioned Talon synthesis.

multiple_comparisons_plan.notes: Sweep space: 3 lookback windows (20, 60, 120 days) × 3 stop-loss levels (5%, 10%, 15%) × 3 profit-target levels (10%, 20%, 30%) = 27 total parameter combinations. Bonferroni correction applied: α_adjusted = 0.05 / 27 ≈ 0.00185. Each variant is treated as an independent test for conservatism. The 27-variant count is consistent with sweep_bounds.max_total_variants and the trial_ledger_budget. Edge family is classified as MOMENTUM by Talon inference; no prior failed packets in this family reduce the effective trial count. Operator accepted all sweep defaults; no operator-confirmed narrowing was applied.
